questions.question: Which of the following is the correct distinction between luminous and non-luminous objects?
options: Luminous objects reflect light, whereas non-luminous objects transmit it.
Luminous objects give out light, whereas non-luminous objects do not.
Luminous objects absorb light, whereas non-luminous objects emit it.
Luminous objects only scatter light, whereas non-luminous objects absorb it.

questions.question: How does the reflection of light from a mirror-like surface differ from its reflection from other everyday surfaces?
options: Mirror-like surfaces absorb all light, while other surfaces reflect it regularly.
Mirror-like surfaces scatter light in all directions, while other surfaces reflect light in a single direction.
Mirror-like surfaces reflect light in a regular way, while other surfaces scatter light.
Mirror-like surfaces do not reflect light, while other surfaces reflect light regularly.

questions.question: Which part of the eye does light pass through to enter, and which light-sensitive part detects it?
options: Light enters through the pupil and is detected by the retina at the back of the eye.
Light enters through the retina and is detected by the pupil at the back of the eye.
Light enters through the iris and is detected by the lens at the front of the eye.
Light enters through the optic nerve and is detected by the cornea.

questions.question: Under what condition can a laser beam or beam of light travelling through the air be seen by an observer?
options: Only if the light beam is travelling through a perfect vacuum.
Only if the light is travelling in a completely straight line without hitting anything.
Only if the light hits particles in the air and reflects or scatters towards the observer's eye.
Only if the beam of light has a frequency that is too low to be absorbed.

questions.question: What is a sound echo, and what type of surface is required to produce it?
options: An echo is a sound that gets absorbed completely by a soft surface.
An echo is a sound heard again after reflecting off a hard surface and travelling back.
An echo is a sound that increases in pitch when it passes through a liquid.
An echo is a sound that stops vibrating when it hits a metal barrier.

questions.question: Why do soft materials absorb a large amount of sound energy?
options: Soft materials contain no particles, preventing sound waves from travelling.
Soft materials reflect sound waves instantly, causing them to lose all energy.
Soft materials increase the frequency of sound until it can no longer be heard.
Sound waves transfer energy to the particles in soft materials, causing them to vibrate.

questions.question: In diagrams showing light reflection, what is the 'normal' line?
options: A physical line drawn parallel to the mirror surface.
An imaginary line drawn at 90 degrees to the surface at the point of reflection.
The path that the incoming light ray takes before hitting the mirror.
The line that represents the boundary between transparent and opaque media.

questions.question: According to the law of reflection, how does the angle of reflection compare to the angle of incidence?
options: The angle of reflection is always double the angle of incidence.
The angle of reflection is always half the angle of incidence.
The angle of reflection is always equal to the angle of incidence, on the other side of the normal.
The angle of reflection is always 90 degrees minus the angle of incidence.

questions.question: Where does the reflection of an object in a flat mirror appear to be located?
options: Directly opposite the object, the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.
Directly opposite the object, twice as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
Slightly to the left of the object, at the surface of the mirror.
Directly behind the observer, at an angle of 90 degrees to the mirror surface.

questions.question: What are the characteristics of an image formed in a flat mirror?
options: It is upside down and laterally inverted.
It is the right way up but is laterally inverted.
It is upside down but not laterally inverted.
It is the right way up and is not laterally inverted.

questions.question: How do transparent and opaque objects differ in how they interact with light?
options: Transparent objects absorb all light, while opaque objects let light travel through them.
Transparent objects reflect all light in a regular way, while opaque objects transmit it.
Transparent objects transmit light through them, while opaque objects do not transmit light.
Transparent objects block light to form shadows, while opaque objects let light pass through.

questions.question: What is a shadow and how is it formed?
options: A bright area formed when light is bent around a transparent object.
An area of high-frequency light caused by reflection off a mirror.
An unlit area in the shape of an object that is blocking light.
A region where light particles are accelerated by a dark surface.

questions.question: What is amplitude, and how does it affect the sound we hear?
options: It is a measure of how fast vibrations occur; a greater amplitude makes a sound higher in pitch.
It is a measure of the size of a vibration; a greater amplitude makes a sound louder.
It is a measure of the speed of sound; a greater amplitude makes sound travel faster.
It is a measure of the distance sound travels; a greater amplitude makes sound quieter.

questions.question: How does the frequency of a vibration affect the pitch of the sound produced?
options: A greater frequency means larger vibrations occur, producing a louder volume.
A greater frequency means fewer vibrations occur, producing a lower pitch.
A greater frequency means vibrations stop completely, producing a quiet sound.
A greater frequency means more vibrations occur per second, producing a higher pitch.

questions.question: Why does sound travel fastest through solids compared to liquids and gases?
options: Solids have strong attractive forces between particles, causing many particles to vibrate when one does.
Solids have particles that are very far apart, allowing sound waves to pass through without hitting them.
Solids have weaker forces holding their particles together, allowing them to vibrate more freely.
Solids absorb sound energy and convert it into light, which travels faster.

questions.question: Why is it impossible for sound to travel through a vacuum, such as outer space?
options: A vacuum has too much gravity, which pulls sound waves down and stops them.
Sound waves require particle vibrations to travel, and there are no particles in a vacuum.
A vacuum absorbs all vibrations and turns them into light rays.
The temperature in a vacuum is too low for sound waves to move.
